display_name: PaddleOCR-VL 1.6 (0.9B) - official doc-parser pipeline + vLLM VLM service
runtime_version: paddleocr 3.6.0 doc_parser pipeline (pipeline_version v1.6, the release default) with the VLM stage served by `paddleocr genai_server --backend vllm`; both come from the official image unmodified - it ships paddleocr[doc-parser]==3.6.0 with paddlex[serving]==3.6.1 and paddlepaddle-gpu==3.2.1 (image config label org.opencontainers.image.version=0006f78-ppocr3.6-pdx3.6, revision 0006f78 = PaddleOCR tag v3.6.0), and v3.6.0 is the release that shipped PaddleOCR-VL-1.6. No paddleocr/paddlex version is installed over the image.
notes: The official docs open by warning that running the 0.9B VLM alone through Transformers, vLLM, SGLang or FastDeploy is NOT equivalent to the PaddleOCR-VL pipeline and produces degraded or hallucinated output. The production path used here is the documented split: the PaddleOCR client keeps layout analysis and the rest of the workflow, and only the VLM stage is delegated to a `paddleocr genai_server --backend vllm` service on loopback. max_concurrency_per_worker is 1 page at a time; block-level parallelism inside a page comes from vl_rec_max_concurrency, matching the historical FOLYNTA c8 configuration. base_image is the official PaddleOCR-VL image, taken unmodified. It is pinned by the version tag the pipeline documentation documents (`paddleocr<major>.<minor>-nvidia-gpu`) plus the digest an anonymous Harbor token read returned on 2026-09-03; `latest-nvidia-gpu` and `0006f78-ppocr3.6-pdx3.6-nvidia-gpu` resolve to the same digest today, and the version tag is used because `latest-*` moves. This file previously claimed the image's paddleocr 3.6.0 predated PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 and installed `paddleocr[doc-parser]==3.7.0` over it. That was wrong and the overlay is removed: PaddleOCR v3.6.0 IS the release that shipped PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 (release notes 2026-05-28), its docs give `pipeline_version` the values v1/v1.5/v1.6 with v1.6 the default, and the image's own build history downloads `PaddleOCR-VL-1.6_infer.tar` and defaults its genai server to `--model_name PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-0.9B`. v3.7.0 released PP-OCRv6, a separate non-VL OCR family, and changes nothing for this pipeline. The Baidu registry publishes no paddleocr3.7-* image on any of paddleocr-vl, paddleocr-genai-vllm-server or paddleocr-genai-fastdeploy-server (full anonymous tag listings, 2026-09-03), so there is nothing newer to move to; every enumeration is recorded in provenance.json. The build and the bootstrap now install only what the official image genuinely lacks and the docs name for it: the prebuilt FlashAttention 2.8.2 wheel (the image ships no nvcc) and `paddleocr install_genai_server_deps vllm`, plus huggingface_hub for the arena's own pinned weight fetch. Both assert the image's paddleocr/paddlex versions fail-closed instead of assuming them. D19/D34 (2026-09-03 second integration pass): this runtime DOES start a model server (`paddleocr genai_server --backend vllm` on loopback), so process ownership lives in entrypoint.sh: the entrypoint renders the launch plan from adapter.py --print-server-plan, starts the server, polls genai_server.ready_probe until it answers (deadline 1200 s, the D19 floor), then runs the worker as a child and traps its own exit to stop the server. The adapter attaches to that server when ARENA_MODEL_SERVER_MANAGED_BY=entrypoint and still starts its own only when nothing else did. prompt_kind is "none": the prompt is fixed inside the official pipeline, adapter.py refuses a non-empty prompt_text, and the registry file is empty. model_repo @ model_revision was re-verified read-only on 2026-09-03 (Hugging Face revision API); runtime_revision is PaddleOCR tag v3.6.0 = commit 0006f787, which the image's own `org.opencontainers.image.revision=0006f78` label confirms it was built from. Framework-floor audit (2026-09-03, after the GLM-OCR canary died on an unrecognised model_type): the required framework floor, what the pinned base image actually ships, the action taken and the evidence URLs are recorded in provenance.json under framework_floor_audit. bootstrap.sh asserts the pinned framework versions and that the framework recognises this checkpoint's architecture before anything starts.
